user_input: I have no rental agreement or receipt. Can I still take action?
expected: Explain alternative evidence (bank debits, chats) without making absolute claims.
actual_response:
[Grounded Statutory AI]

### 📋 Your Legal Position and Available Options

**1. What Your Situation Involves:**
Based on what you've shared, this involves Security deposit withholding regarding ₹35,000.

**2. Applicable Legal Provisions:**
- **[The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 — Section 106](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/2338?view_type=browse&sam_handle=123456789/1362)**: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
- **[The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 — Section 12](https://nalsa.gov.in/)**: Criteria for giving legal services (Free Legal Aid via NALSA / SLSA / DLSA)
- Under Indian law, arbitrary retention of funds without verifiable itemized loss is legally unsustainable.
- In tenancy disputes, routine painting and standard aging fall under reasonable wear and tear (Transfer of Property Act, 1882 Section 108).
- In consumer matters, refusal to replace or refund for defective products is an Unfair Trade Practice under Section 2(47) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

**3. Practical Evidence to Preserve:**
- Bank/UPI payment receipts.
- Date-stamped photographs or handover videos.
- Written communications (WhatsApp/emails).

**4. Recommended Action:**
- Send a formal written demand notice with an explicit 15-day compliance window.
- If unresolved, proceed to pre-litigation conciliation via the National Consumer Helpline (1915), state Rent Authority, or Labour Commissioner.

citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.
